status: Unresolved; R04 remains excluded from fit. No new Hay River location accepted.
observations: Northern trial R04 lies amid river, mill, road and railway ink. Its original376m discrepancy is retained as provisional, not survey truth.

C14 historical southern tributary extends through a small oval feature and farther south; modern198990 terminates after about318m in a swamp area. This difference is not enough to infer when or why drainage changed, or to identify a better modern point.

A second historical northern tributary occurs farther west near the mill/railway. It distinguishes the Schoolhouse Brook junction J0571 from the upstream northern tributary trial; shifting R04 to J0571 solely for proximity would confuse their order. The western source intersection is itself obscured by railway/mill detail and was not accepted as another precise point.

rejected_alternatives.proposal: Move R04 to J0571 / shift the entire Hay River point sequence west
rejected_alternatives.reason: Does not preserve the two northern tributaries and their order relative to southern arms; no fitting trial adopted.

rejected_alternatives.proposal: Fit R04 with the existing two southern controls
rejected_alternatives.reason: Prior reproducible raster failure: severe compression and78496 missing interior cells; no new evidence justifies retrying the same constraint.

next_evidence_needed: An independently dated reference or clearer native interpretation that identifies the northern tributary/mill channels and southern pond drainage. Do not infer real channel change from mismatch alone.
correction: The initial rejection of a westward identity correction was premature: F05 south arm is the Hays main, not a second southern tributary. Native topology re-audit with the dated NRCan map resolves the sequence as MacKays, Schoolhouse, MacKinnons, unnamed northern tributary. Retained here as investigation history, not current interpretation.
